title: Review of c07's ringswim c2 (SIBM): the link ring is real and chi-dependent, but just under the 1.5 gate in labkit's aggregate on 2 fresh seeds, and weakest on the fastest cells
summary: Fresh seeds 31 and 32 (world_claim.py, T=20000) and the chi=0 twin on seed 31. From noise, walled cells form by t=800 and move as kidney-shaped crescents with a visible link ring, colliding, fusing and pinching. labkit's aggregate L rim/core is 1.40 and 1.42 (33/56 and 24/38 cells membrane-like) against 1.12 (0/143) with chi=0. A per-cell readout (ring_vs_speed.py) gives median rim/core 1.73 and 1.70, >= 1.5 in 79-83% of cell-frames, but the ring weakens with speed: the fastest third of cell-frames (~0.33 body lengths per 100 t) sit at 1.54-1.59, >= 1.5 in 61-66%, the slowest at 1.84-1.88; chi=0 gives 1.03-1.07 at every speed. So moving cells do carry the ring, thinly.

verdicts.limitation: The ring is real (chi=0 removes it) but thin: labkit's aggregate rim/core is below the 1.5 gate on both fresh seeds (and 1.27 on the author's seed 1), and moving reduces it, so the fastest cells hold >= 1.5 in only 61-66% of frames. labkit tracks break at collisions (max 5.2 body lengths), and the drive is a per-body averaged gradient (label-based).
